creator: alanonai
title: Should you use Supabase when AI recommends it? Vendor lock-in considerations and how to abstract DB/auth to keep migration possible

tools.name: Supabase
tools.detail: Postgres DB + auth + backend/edge functions bundle that AI tools default to recommending

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.detail: keep DB calls as plain Postgres so they port off Supabase

claims: AI recommends Supabase because it bundles DB, auth (one of the hardest parts), backend functions, and is easy to configure -- AI optimises for easy
Once locked into a vendor, migrating means changing DB, auth and backend functions at once; harder as the app and customer base grow
Three questions before locking in: consumers vs businesses (business requirements Supabase may not naturally handle), compliance requirements, very complex backend logic
Answer is 'it depends'; Supabase is still a good service
how_to_steps: When AI suggests Supabase, have a conversation with the AI about lock-in before accepting
Ask: B2C or B2B? compliance needs? complex backend logic?
If adopting, abstract database calls so they are plain Postgres SQL
Abstract the authentication layer behind an interface so a different auth provider can be swapped in later

relevance.why: Directly applicable: Claude Code defaults to Supabase for new apps. The abstraction advice (plain Postgres, auth behind an interface) is a cheap hedge against lock-in that a solo founder should bake into CLAUDE.md.

implement_score.why: Add two rules to project CLAUDE.md: keep DB access as standard Postgres via a repository layer, and wrap auth behind a single module. Minimal cost now, large savings if a B2B/compliance customer forces a migration.
